Michael Wilson, also known by his Insta-Handle, Hellcat Mike, was taken to Fort Bend County Jail and charged with evading arrest and possession of a controlled substance between 200 and 400 grams, Penalty Group 3. In Texas, a Penalty Group 3 drug is a substance that has an accepted medical use as well as a mid-level potential for abuse, such as anabolic steroids, Xanax, and Ritalin. Though he was originally denied bail due to his extensive criminal history, Michael's lawyer successfully argued that denying bail was a violation of Michael's constitutional rights. The court then set his bail at $250,000 and required Michael to wear a GPS monitor and to remain at home, except for court appointments. After alleged violations of his bond agreement, his bail was revoked in April 2024. In May, the court set his bond at an aggregate $700,000. Michael entered a plea agreement and pleaded guilty to evading arrest in exchange for dropping the drug charge. Michael waived his right for his sentence to be decided by a jury, and instead opted for the judge to decide his fate. After the judge saw Michael's Instagram account, featuring other videos of Michael advertising Hellcats by running from the police, he sentenced him to 10 years in prison. After his conviction, a bench warrant from Bear County was issued, where, according to court documents, he will stand trial for engaging in organized criminal activity, allegedly stemming from a chop shop that he ran in San Antonio as the leader of a four-man car theft ring. Michael is also due to be sentenced after pleading guilty to evading arrest in Guadalupe County.
